claim: Aldh1a1 is expressed in the dorsal neural retina at E12.5, not in the RPE and choroid complex.
source: At E12.5, Aldh1a1 was localized in the progenitor cells at the dorsal neural retina, and no Aldh1a1 expression was observed in the RPE and choroid complex (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Aldh1a3 is mainly localized in the ventral region of the retina and RPE at E12.5.
source: At E12.5, Aldh1a1 (green) and Aldh1a3 (red) are expressed in dorsal and ventral neural retina (NR), respectively. At the dorsal edge (white box), Aldh1a1 is expressed only in NR, not in RPE (right upper panel), while some RPE cells are Aldh1a3-positive (right lower panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: At E17.5, Aldh1a1 expression is observed in the dorsal region and the ventral edge of the retina, but not in the RPE/choroid complex.
source: At E17.5, Aldh1a1 expression was observed in the dorsal region and the ventral edge, but no expression was detected in the RPE/choroid complex (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B and described in the text.

claim: In adult tissue, Aldh1a1-positive cells are preferentially localized in the middle of the inner nuclear layer cells and spread to the dorsal region of the retina.
source: In adult tissue, in situ hybridization showed that Aldh1a1-positive cells were preferentially localized in the middle of the inner nuclear layer (INL) cells, and had spread to the dorsal region of the retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B and described in the text.

claim: Aldh1a1-positive cells are observed at the ventral edge of the adult retina.
source: We also observed Aldh1a1-positive cells at the ventral edge of the adult retina (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1C and described in the text.

claim: Aldh1a1 colocalizes with glutamine synthetase (GS), a marker of Müller glia, in adult retina.
source: Immunohistochemistry of sectioned tissues showed Aldh1a1 colocalized with glutamine synthetase (GS), a marker of Müller glia.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data described in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Aldh1a1 is preferentially expressed in retinal progenitor cells of the dorsal region from the embryonic stage.
source: These results indicate that Aldh1a1 is preferentially expressed in the retinal progenitor cells of the dorsal region from the embryonic stage, and in Müller cells in the dorsal region and the ventral edge of the retina in adulthood.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization data presented in Figures 1A-C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Aldh1a1 is expressed in Müller cells in the dorsal region and the ventral edge of the retina in adulthood.
source: These results indicate that Aldh1a1 is preferentially expressed in the retinal progenitor cells of the dorsal region from the embryonic stage, and in Müller cells in the dorsal region and the ventral edge of the retina in adulthood.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization data presented in Figures 1A-C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adult Aldh1a1–/– mice display a loss of pigmentation in the dorsonasal area of the eyeballs.
source: In adult Aldh1a1–/– mice, the eyeballs displayed a loss of pigmentation in the dorsonasal area (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observation shown in Figure 1D and described in the text.

claim: Pigmentation is lost from the choroidal region, not from RPE cells, in Aldh1a1–/– mice.
source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H and E) staining of the paraffin sections revealed that pigmentation was lost from the choroidal region, not from RPE cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining data shown in Figure 1E and described in the text.

claim: The choroidal thickness in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes is significantly less than that of the dorsal and ventral sides of WT eyes and the ventral side of Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
source: The choroidal thickness was significantly less than that of the dorsal and ventral sides of WT eyes and the ventral side of Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation of choroidal thickness shown in Figure 1F and described in the text.

claim: There are no obvious morphological differences in the thickness of the neural retina in Aldh1a1–/– mice compared to WT.
source: There were no obvious morphological differences in the thickness of the neural retina or in the length of the outer segments of photoreceptor cells (Figure 1G and H), as reported previously (Fan et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 1G and described in the text, and also cites previous work.

claim: There are no obvious morphological differences in the length of the outer segments of photoreceptor cells in Aldh1a1–/– mice compared to WT.
source: There were no obvious morphological differences in the thickness of the neural retina or in the length of the outer segments of photoreceptor cells (Figure 1G and H), as reported previously (Fan et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 1H and described in the text, and also cites previous work.

claim: The choroidal vessels of Aldh1a1–/– mice are hypoplastic.
source: These findings suggest that the choroidal vessels of Aldh1a1–/– mice are hypoplastic.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the morphological observations of reduced choroidal thickness and loss of pigmentation in Aldh1a1–/– mice.

claim: Aldh1a1–/– mice exhibited choroidal hypoplasia in the dorsal region of the eyes.
source: Surprisingly, the Aldh1a1–/– mice exhibited choroidal hypoplasia in the dorsal region of the eyes (Figure 2A), although Aldh1a1 is normally expressed in the neural retina.
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2A and described in the text.

claim: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, fewer choroidal vessels with more avascular areas were detected compared to WT.
source: In the dorsal and ventral regions of WT and the ventral region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, the choriocapillaris was normal, with a dense mesh structure, whereas fewer choroidal vessels with more avascular areas were detected in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-magnification Z-stack images shown in Figure 2B and C and described in the text.

claim: The vascular density in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes is significantly lower than that in other regions.
source: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, the vascular density was significantly lower than that in the other regions (Figure 2E), whereas there were no significant morphological differences in the localization of ZO-1 signals and RPE size between WT and Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation of vascular density shown in Figure 2E and described in the text.

claim: There are no significant morphological differences in the localization of ZO-1 signals and RPE size between WT and Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
source: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, the vascular density was significantly lower than that in the other regions (Figure 2E), whereas there were no significant morphological differences in the localization of ZO-1 signals and RPE size between WT and Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by whole-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 2D and F and described in the text.

claim: Aldh1a1–/– eyes show choroidal hypoplasia without degeneration of the RPE in the dorsal region.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that Aldh1a1–/– eyes show choroidal hypoplasia without degeneration of the RPE in the dorsal region.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the immunohistochemistry data showing reduced vascular density but normal RPE morphology in Aldh1a1–/– eyes.

claim: Aldh1a1–/– eyes exhibit apparently normal morphology of photoreceptor and RPE cells, despite the complete absence of choroidal pigmentation and the presence of a thin dorsal choroid layer.
source: The TEM images demonstrated that Aldh1a1–/– eyes exhibited apparently normal morphology of photoreceptor and RPE cells, despite the complete absence of choroidal pigmentation and the presence of a thin dorsal choroid layer (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3A and described in the text.

claim: Bruch's membrane does not differ significantly between WT and Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
source: Bruch's membrane did not differ significantly between WT and Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3B and described in the text.

claim: The choroidal vessels in the hypoplastic dorsal section of Aldh1a1–/– eyes show fenestrations, a characteristic of capillaries.
source: Remarkably, the choroidal vessels in the hypoplastic dorsal section of Aldh1a1–/– eyes showed fenestrations, a characteristic of capillaries, as did those in the dorsal and ventral regions of WT and the ventral region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3C and described in the text.

claim: The hypoplastic blood vessels of the Aldh1a1–/– eyes maintain the characteristics of the choriocapillaris, including an intact RPE and Bruch's membrane.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the hypoplastic blood vessels of the Aldh1a1–/– eyes maintain the characteristics of the choriocapillaris, including an intact RPE and Bruch's membrane.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the transmission electron microscopy data showing fenestrations in the hypoplastic vessels and normal RPE and Bruch's membrane morphology.

claim: In WT choroidal flat-mounts, the choriocapillaris coexpresses both Flt1-DsRed and Kdr-EGFP, while the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels express only Flt1-DsRed.
source: In the choroidal flat-mounts from adult WT mice, the choriocapillaris coexpressed both Flt1-DsRed and Kdr-EGFP, while the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels expressed only Flt1-DsRed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Z-stack images of choroidal flat-mounts shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D and described in the text.

claim: More Flt1-DsRed appears to be expressed in the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels than in the choriocapillaris in WT mice.
source: In addition, more Flt1-DsRed appeared to be expressed in the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels than in the choriocapillaris (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Z-stack images of choroidal flat-mounts shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and described in the text.

claim: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, all the blood vessels associated with the hypoplastic choroid coexpress both Flt1-DsRed and Kdr-EGFP.
source: In contrast, in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, all the blood vessels associated with the hypoplastic choroid coexpressed both Flt1-DsRed and Kdr-EGFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Z-stack images of choroidal flat-mounts shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D and described in the text.

claim: The level of expression of Flt1-tdsRed in the Aldh1a1–/– blood vessels appears lower than that in the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels.
source: Also, the level of expression of Flt1-tdsRed in the Aldh1a1–/– blood vessels appeared lower than that in the medium-sized/large choroidal vessels.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of fluorescence intensity in the images shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The formation of the choroidal vascular network starts at approximately E13.5.
source: Since the formation of the choroidal vascular network starts at approximately E13.5 (Zhao and Overbeek, 2001; Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006), we compared the vascular development in the choroid of the eyes of WT and Aldh1a1–/– mice from E16.5 to postnatal (P)28 using a choroidal flat-mounts immunostained with antibodies against endomucin and ETS-related gene (ERG), which are enriched in endothelial cells (Figure 4A; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Zhao and Overbeek, 2001; Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).

claim: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes at E16.5, endomucin immunostaining is patchy, indicating that choroidal hypoplasia is already detectable.
source: In the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes, endomucin immunostaining was patchy, indicating that choroidal hypoplasia was already detectable (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 4A and B and described in the text.

claim: There are significantly fewer endothelial cells in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– eyes at E16.5 compared to WT eyes.
source: There were significantly fewer endothelial cells in the area than in WT eyes (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation of ERG-positive cells shown in Figure 4C and described in the text.

claim: VEGF levels in the Aldh1a1–/– RPE-choroid complex are significantly lower than those in WT eyes at E17.5 and P24.
source: VEGF levels in the Aldh1a1–/– RPE-choroid complex were significantly lower than those in WT eyes at both time points (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA analysis shown in Figure 4D and described in the text.

claim: Vegfa mRNA expression of the E16.5 Aldh1a1−/− RPE cells is reduced at the dorsal half where Aldh1a1 is expressed in the WT neural retina.
source: In addition, in situ hybridization revealed that Vegfa mRNA expression of the E16.5 Aldh1a1−/− RPE cells was reduced at the dorsal half where Aldh1a1 is expressed in the WT neural retina (Figure 4E, shown as arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 4E and described in the text.

claim: RAs significantly enhance VEGF secretion in primary human RPE cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As a result, RAs significantly enhanced VEGF secretion in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA analysis of RA-treated primary human RPE cells shown in Figure 4F and described in the text.

claim: VAD mice show dorsal choroidal hypoplasia at P3.
source: At P3, VAD mice showed dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in the flat-mount analysis (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 4G and described in the text.

claim: In the dorsal region of VAD eyes, the vascular density is significantly lower than that in other regions.
source: In the dorsal region of VAD eyes, the vascular density was significantly lower than that in the other regions such as the dorsal and ventral regions of WT and the ventral region of VAD eyes (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative evaluation of vascular density shown in Figure 4H and described in the text.

claim: RA administration to pregnant Aldh1a1–/– mice from E10 to E16 significantly suppresses the dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in their offspring.
source: Also, RA administration to pregnant Aldh1a1–/– mice by oral gavage from E10 to E16 significantly suppressed the dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in their offspring (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 4I and J and described in the text.

claim: RA controls dorsal choroidal vascular development.
source: These results indicate that RA controls dorsal choroidal vascular development and that dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in Aldh1a1–/– mice is causally related to a deficiency in RA synthesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that VAD mice have dorsal choroidal hypoplasia and that RA administration rescues the phenotype in Aldh1a1–/– mice.

claim: Dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in Aldh1a1–/– mice is causally related to a deficiency in RA synthesis.
source: These results indicate that RA controls dorsal choroidal vascular development and that dorsal choroidal hypoplasia in Aldh1a1–/– mice is causally related to a deficiency in RA synthesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that VAD mice have dorsal choroidal hypoplasia and that RA administration rescues the phenotype in Aldh1a1–/– mice.

claim: Aldh1a3 begins to be expressed in the entire RPE cell layer and in the ventral region of the neural retina from E10.5.
source: These observations raised the question of whether Aldh1a3, another RA-producing enzyme in the mouse retina, also affects choroidal vascularization, because Aldh1a3 begins to be expressed in the entire RPE cell layer and in the ventral region of the neural retina from E10.5 (Matt et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Matt et al., 2005).

claim: Conditional disruption of Aldh1a3 in the neural retina does not affect choriocapillaris development.
source: To test this possibility, we conditionally disrupted Aldh1a3 in the neural retina (floxed Aldh1a3 mice crossed with Pax6-α-Cre), however, in these mice, choriocapillaris development was found to be normal (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and described in the text.

claim: RAs derived from Aldh1a1 but not Aldh1a3 control choroidal vascular development by enhancing VEGF secretion from RPE cells.
source: In conclusion, RAs derived from Aldh1a1 but not Aldh1a3 control choroidal vascular development by enhancing VEGF secretion from RPE cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that Aldh1a1–/– mice have choroidal hypoplasia and reduced VEGF, while Aldh1a3 conditional knockout mice have normal choriocapillaris development.

claim: Conditional disruption of Pax6 in the RPE at the early embryonic stages results in the loss of pigmentation.
source: Recently, it was reported that conditional disruption of Pax6 in the RPE at the early embryonic stages resulted in the loss of pigmentation (Raviv et al., 2014), and Pax6 conditional knockout mice in which the Vegfa promoter is synergistically transactivated by Pax6 and Sox9 exhibit choroidal hypoplasia (Cohen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Raviv et al., 2014).

claim: Pax6 conditional knockout mice in which the Vegfa promoter is synergistically transactivated by Pax6 and Sox9 exhibit choroidal hypoplasia.
source: Recently, it was reported that conditional disruption of Pax6 in the RPE at the early embryonic stages resulted in the loss of pigmentation (Raviv et al., 2014), and Pax6 conditional knockout mice in which the Vegfa promoter is synergistically transactivated by Pax6 and Sox9 exhibit choroidal hypoplasia (Cohen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cohen et al., 2016).

claim: The intensity of Pax6 immunofluorescence in the dorsal Aldh1a1–/– RPE is slightly lower than WT at E12.5 and E14.5, but does not show a significant difference.
source: The intensity of Pax6 immunofluorescence in the dorsal Aldh1a1–/– RPE was slightly lower than WT at E12.5 and E14.5, but did not show a significant difference (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C and described in the text.

claim: In the E12.5 WT neural retina, Sox9 is predominantly expressed in the dorsal region rather than in the ventral region.
source: In the E12.5 WT neural retina, Sox9 was predominantly expressed in the dorsal region rather than in the ventral region, and the expression level at the dorsal region became comparable to the ventral region at E14.5.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A and described in the text.

claim: The expression level of Sox9 at the dorsal region of the neural retina becomes comparable to the ventral region at E14.5 in WT mice.
source: In the E12.5 WT neural retina, Sox9 was predominantly expressed in the dorsal region rather than in the ventral region, and the expression level at the dorsal region became comparable to the ventral region at E14.5.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A and described in the text.

claim: In Aldh1a1–/– neural retinas, Sox9 immunofluorescence in the dorsal region is reduced as much as that of the ventral region.
source: In Aldh1a1–/– neural retinas, Sox9 immunofluorescence in the dorsal region was reduced as much as that of the ventral region (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 5A and C and described in the text.

claim: In the E12.5 WT RPE cells, there is no difference in Sox9 immunofluorescence between dorsal and ventral region.
source: In the E12.5 WT RPE cells, there was no difference in Sox9 immunofluorescence between dorsal and ventral region, and the intensity increased at E14.5.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B and D and described in the text.

claim: The intensity of Sox9 immunofluorescence in WT RPE cells increases at E14.5.
source: In the E12.5 WT RPE cells, there was no difference in Sox9 immunofluorescence between dorsal and ventral region, and the intensity increased at E14.5.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B and E and described in the text.

claim: In the E12.5 Aldh1a1–/– RPE cells, the Sox9 immunofluorescence is comparable to WT.
source: In the E12.5 Aldh1a1–/– RPE cells, the immunofluorescence was comparable to WT, but was significantly lower than that of E14.5 WT (Figure 5B,D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 5B and D and described in the text.

claim: In the E14.5 Aldh1a1–/– RPE cells, the Sox9 immunofluorescence is significantly lower than that of E14.5 WT.
source: In the E12.5 Aldh1a1–/– RPE cells, the immunofluorescence was comparable to WT, but was significantly lower than that of E14.5 WT (Figure 5B,D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 5B and E and described in the text.

claim: Aldh1a1 enhances Sox9 expression in the dorsal neural retina and RPE cells during development.
source: These densitometry results suggest that Aldh1a1 enhances Sox9 expression in the dorsal neural retina and RPE cells during development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation data showing reduced Sox9 expression in Aldh1a1–/– neural retina and RPE cells.

claim: RA exposure enhances both Sox9 and Vegfa mRNA expression in primary RPE cells.
source: The results showed that both Sox9 and Vegfa mRNAs (Figure 5F and G) were enhanced in an RA-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5F and G and described in the text.

claim: Overexpression of Sox9 results in upregulation of Vegfa mRNA in primary RPE cells.
source: Overexpression of Sox9 by transient transfection of a pCAGIG-Sox9 vector resulted in upregulation of Vegfa mRNA (Figure 5H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5H and I and described in the text.

claim: Knockdown of Sox9 results in downregulation of Vegfa mRNA in primary RPE cells.
source: In contrast, knockdown by transient transfection of Sox9 siRNA resulted in downregulation of Vegfa mRNA (Figure 5J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5J and K and described in the text.

claim: Sox9 enhanced by Aldh1a1-mediated RA upregulates Vegfa expression in RPE cells.
source: Taken together, these results strongly suggest that Sox9 enhanced by Aldh1a1-mediated RA upregulates Vegfa expression in RPE cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that RA enhances Sox9 and Vegfa expression, and that Sox9 overexpression/knockdown affects Vegfa expression in RPE cells.

claim: mCherry expression from E16.5 Tyr-Cre mice is observed in all RPE.
source: In the Cre-reporter assay with R26R-H2B-mCherry mice (Abe et al., 2011) on an albino background, mCherry expression from E16.5 Tyr-Cre mice was observed in all RPE, although a few mCherry-positive cells were found in the neural retina (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Cre-reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and described in the text.

claim: A few mCherry-positive cells are found in the neural retina of E16.5 Tyr-Cre mice.
source: In the Cre-reporter assay with R26R-H2B-mCherry mice (Abe et al., 2011) on an albino background, mCherry expression from E16.5 Tyr-Cre mice was observed in all RPE, although a few mCherry-positive cells were found in the neural retina (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Cre-reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and described in the text.

claim: mCherry expression in Pax6-α-Cre mice is restricted to the dorsal and ventral portions of the neural retina.
source: Also, mCherry expression in Pax6-α-Cre mice was restricted to the dorsal and ventral portions of the neural retina as reported previously (Marquardt et al., 2001), but no mCherry-positive cells were found in the choroid (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Cre-reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and described in the text, and also cites previous work.

claim: No mCherry-positive cells are found in the choroid of Pax6-α-Cre mice.
source: Also, mCherry expression in Pax6-α-Cre mice was restricted to the dorsal and ventral portions of the neural retina as reported previously (Marquardt et al., 2001), but no mCherry-positive cells were found in the choroid (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Cre-reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and described in the text.

claim: RPE-specific conditional knockout of Sox9 shows less pigmentation in the dorsal region.
source: In RPE-cKO of Sox9, we found less pigmentation in the dorsal region, and significantly poorer vasculature in the dorsal choroidal area than the other areas (Figure 6A and B), which phenocopied Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 6A and B and described in the text.

claim: RPE-specific conditional knockout of Sox9 shows significantly poorer vasculature in the dorsal choroidal area than the other areas.
source: In RPE-cKO of Sox9, we found less pigmentation in the dorsal region, and significantly poorer vasculature in the dorsal choroidal area than the other areas (Figure 6A and B), which phenocopied Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 6A and B and described in the text.

claim: RPE-specific conditional knockout of Sox9 phenocopies Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
source: In RPE-cKO of Sox9, we found less pigmentation in the dorsal region, and significantly poorer vasculature in the dorsal choroidal area than the other areas (Figure 6A and B), which phenocopied Aldh1a1–/– eyes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that RPE-cKO of Sox9 shows similar phenotypes to Aldh1a1–/– eyes.

claim: Although Sox9 is disrupted in all RPE cells in RPE-cKO of Sox9, the poor vasculature phenotype is restricted to the dorsal region.
source: Interestingly, although Sox9 was disrupted in all RPE cells, the poor vasculature phenotype was restricted to the dorsal region, and did not appear in the ventral region (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 6B and described in the text.

claim: Retina-specific conditional knockout of Sox9 shows no hypoplasia of the choroidal vasculature or lack of pigmentation.
source: Conversely, Retina-cKO of Sox9 showed no hypoplasia of the choroidal vasculature or lack of pigmentation (Figure 6A and B), indicating that Sox9 in the neural retina is not responsible for choroidal vascular development.
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 6A and B and described in the text.

claim: Sox9 in the neural retina is not responsible for choroidal vascular development.
source: Conversely, Retina-cKO of Sox9 showed no hypoplasia of the choroidal vasculature or lack of pigmentation (Figure 6A and B), indicating that Sox9 in the neural retina is not responsible for choroidal vascular development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Retina-cKO of Sox9 shows no choroidal phenotype.

claim: Tyr-Cre-induced overexpression of Sox9 significantly recovers the choroidal hypoplasia phenotypes in the dorsal region of Aldh1a1–/– mice.
source: Tyr-Cre-induced overexpression of Sox9 in these mice significantly recovered the choroidal hypoplasia phenotypes in the dorsal region (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by choroidal flat-mount immunohistochemistry and quantitative evaluation shown in Figure 6C and D and described in the text.

claim: Sox9 expression enhanced by Aldh1a1 in developing RPE cells is critical for normal choroidal vasculature development.
source: These results indicated that Sox9 expression enhanced by Aldh1a1 in developing RPE cells is critical for normal choroidal vasculature development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that RPE-cKO of Sox9 phenocopies Aldh1a1–/– eyes and that Sox9 overexpression rescues the phenotype.

claim: The choroid is the primary nutrient source for the retina.
source: The primary nutrient source for the retina is the choroid (Bill et al., 1980), which is a highly vascularized tissue layer surrounding the retina.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Bill et al., 1980).

claim: The choroid is a highly vascularized tissue layer surrounding the retina.
source: The primary nutrient source for the retina is the choroid (Bill et al., 1980), which is a highly vascularized tissue layer surrounding the retina.
evidence: The claim is based on established anatomical knowledge and supported by citation.

claim: The choroid consists of three layers: Haller's layer (large blood vessel layer), Sattler's layer (medium size blood vessels), and the choriocapillaris.
source: The choroid consists of three layers: Haller's layer (large blood vessel layer), Sattler's layer (medium size blood vessels), and the choriocapillaris (Hogan et al., 1971; Nickla and Wallman, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hogan et al., 1971; Nickla and Wallman, 2010).

claim: The choriocapillaris is a unique anastomosed vascular structure with an extraretinal fenestrated capillary bed that lies in a single plane below Bruch's membrane.
source: The choriocapillaris is a unique anastomosed vascular structure with an extraretinal fenestrated capillary bed that lies in a single plane below Bruch's membrane.
evidence: The claim is based on established anatomical knowledge.

claim: In the mouse retina, choroidal development begins from embryonic day (E)13.5.
source: In the mouse retina, choroidal development begins from embryonic day (E)13.5 (Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).

claim: VEGF is a central regulator of vascular development during embryogenesis.
source: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is known to be a central regulator of vascular development during embryogenesis (Coultas et al., 2005), and VEGF secreted from RPE cells is indispensable for the vascular development and maintenance of the choroid (Saint-Geniez et al., 2009; Le et al., 2010; Kurihara et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Coultas et al., 2005).

claim: VEGF secreted from RPE cells is indispensable for the vascular development and maintenance of the choroid.
source: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is known to be a central regulator of vascular development during embryogenesis (Coultas et al., 2005), and VEGF secreted from RPE cells is indispensable for the vascular development and maintenance of the choroid (Saint-Geniez et al., 2009; Le et al., 2010; Kurihara et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Saint-Geniez et al., 2009; Le et al., 2010; Kurihara et al., 2012).

claim: VEGF expression is enhanced by a number of transcription factors such as hypoxia-induced factor-1α (HIF-1α), estrogen-related receptor-α (ERRα), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coreceptor 1α (PGC-1α).
source: VEGF expression is enhanced by a number of transcription factors such as hypoxia-induced factor-1α (HIF-1α), estrogen-related receptor-α (ERRα), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coreceptor 1α (PGC-1α) (Ziello et al., 2007; Ueta et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Ziello et al., 2007; Ueta et al., 2012).

claim: Aldh1a1 is an enzyme that synthesizes retinoic acids (RAs).
source: Aldh1a1 is an enzyme that synthesizes retinoic acids (RAs) and is expressed in the dorsal neural retina from the embryonic stage, not in the RPE and the choroid (Matt et al., 2005; Molotkov et al., 2006; Luo et al., 2006; Kumar et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on established biochemical knowledge and supported by citations.

claim: Aldh1a1 is expressed in the dorsal neural retina from the embryonic stage, not in the RPE and the choroid.
source: Aldh1a1 is an enzyme that synthesizes retinoic acids (RAs) and is expressed in the dorsal neural retina from the embryonic stage, not in the RPE and the choroid (Matt et al., 2005; Molotkov et al., 2006; Luo et al., 2006; Kumar et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Matt et al., 2005; Molotkov et al., 2006; Luo et al., 2006; Kumar et al., 2012).

claim: RAs are essential for biological activities such as reproduction, development, growth, and maintenance.
source: RAs are essential for biological activities such as reproduction, development, growth, and maintenance (Kam et al., 2012; Rhinn and Dollé, 2012; Cunningham and Duester, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Kam et al., 2012; Rhinn and Dollé, 2012; Cunningham and Duester, 2015).

claim: Aldh1a1 is expressed in the dorsal region of embryonic and adult retinas.
source: It was previously reported that Aldh1a1 is expressed in the dorsal region of embryonic and adult retinas (McCaffery et al., 1991; Fan et al., 2003; Matt et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (McCaffery et al., 1991; Fan et al., 2003; Matt et al., 2005).

claim: Previous developmental and electrophysiological analyses of the Aldh1a1–/– mouse have shown that the neural retina is apparently normal.
source: Previous developmental and electrophysiological analyses of the Aldh1a1–/– mouse has shown that the neural retina is apparently normal (Fan et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Fan et al., 2003).

claim: CD31-positive endothelial cells and VEGF expression in mouse eyes can be observed in choroid and primitive RPE cells at E10.5.
source: CD31-positive endothelial cells and VEGF expression in mouse eyes can be observed in choroid and primitive RPE cells at E10.5 (Saint-Geniez et al., 2006), and choroidal vascular development is initiated at E11.5 when periocular vessels emerge following formation of the vascular network at around E13.5 (Zhao and Overbeek, 2001; Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).

claim: Choroidal vascular development is initiated at E11.5 when periocular vessels emerge following formation of the vascular network at around E13.5.
source: CD31-positive endothelial cells and VEGF expression in mouse eyes can be observed in choroid and primitive RPE cells at E10.5 (Saint-Geniez et al., 2006), and choroidal vascular development is initiated at E11.5 when periocular vessels emerge following formation of the vascular network at around E13.5 (Zhao and Overbeek, 2001; Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Zhao and Overbeek, 2001; Marneros et al., 2005; Saint-Geniez et al., 2006).

claim: Conditional disruption of Vegfa in RPE cells at E10 or E13 results in decreased choroidal vascular density.
source: Although conditional disruption of Vegfa in RPE cells at E10 or E13 resulted in decreased choroidal vascular density, loss of the RPE-produced VEGF after E15 caused no significant defects in the choroidal vasculature (Le et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Le et al., 2010).

claim: Loss of the RPE-produced VEGF after E15 causes no significant defects in the choroidal vasculature.
source: Although conditional disruption of Vegfa in RPE cells at E10 or E13 resulted in decreased choroidal vascular density, loss of the RPE-produced VEGF after E15 caused no significant defects in the choroidal vasculature (Le et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Le et al., 2010).

claim: Aldh1a1 expression during E10 to E13 in trans potentiates VEGF secretion from RPE cells to allow the development of normal choroidal vascularization.
source: Together with our demonstration that choroidal VEGF production is downregulated in Aldh1a1–/– embryos, these data suggest that Aldh1a1 expression during E10 to E13 in trans potentiates VEGF secretion from RPE cells to allow the development of normal choroidal vascularization.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing reduced VEGF in Aldh1a1–/– embryos and the known timing of choroidal vascular development.

claim: Severe choriocapillaris vasoconstriction occurs in adult tamoxifen-induced Vegfflox/flox;VMD2-Cre mice.
source: Considering that severe choriocapillaris vasoconstriction occurs in adult tamoxifen-induced Vegfflox/flox;VMD2-Cre mice (Kurihara et al., 2012), it is possible that Aldh1a1 is also responsible for maintenance of the choriocapillaris.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kurihara et al., 2012).

claim: It is possible that Aldh1a1 is also responsible for maintenance of the choriocapillaris.
source: Considering that severe choriocapillaris vasoconstriction occurs in adult tamoxifen-induced Vegfflox/flox;VMD2-Cre mice (Kurihara et al., 2012), it is possible that Aldh1a1 is also responsible for maintenance of the choriocapillaris.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observation that choroidal VEGF level is still reduced at P24 in Aldh1a1–/– mice and the known role of VEGF in choriocapillaris maintenance.

claim: Aldh1a1-mediated RA is responsible for normal choroidal vascular formation by controlling VEGF secretion from RPE cells.
source: These results strongly suggest that Aldh1a1-mediated RA is responsible for normal choroidal vascular formation by controlling VEGF secretion from RPE cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that RAs enhance VEGF secretion from primary RPE cells, VAD mice have choroidal hypoplasia, and RA administration rescues the phenotype in Aldh1a1–/– mice.

claim: Aldh1a1-mediated RA production stimulates Sox9 expression in dorsal RPE cells and Sox9 then transactivates the Vegfa promoter.
source: Considering that in primary RPE cells RA exposure enhances both Sox9 and Vegfa expression and that overexpression and knockdown of Sox9 influences Vegfa expression, it is more likely that Aldh1a1-mediated RA production stimulates Sox9 expression in dorsal RPE cells and Sox9 then transactivates the Vegfa promoter.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that RA enhances Sox9 and Vegfa expression, and that Sox9 overexpression/knockdown affects Vegfa expression in RPE cells.

claim: Retinoic acid receptor α (RARα) and retinoid X receptor α (RXRα) are expressed in RPE cells at an early embryonic stage.
source: Retinoic acid receptor α (RARα) and retinoid X receptor α (RXRα) are expressed in RPE cells at an early embryonic stage (Mori et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Mori et al., 2001).

claim: It is plausible that RARα and RXRα enhance Sox9 expression in dorsal RPE cells.
source: It is plausible that RARα and RXRα enhance Sox9 expression in dorsal RPE cells, although the precise molecular mechanism remains to be investigated.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the known expression of RARα and RXRα in RPE cells and the observation that RA enhances Sox9 expression.

claim: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of severe vision loss in humans.
source: For example, age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of severe vision loss in humans (de Jong, 2006) and is caused by abnormalities of the subfoveal choriocapillaris.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (de Jong, 2006).

claim: AMD is caused by abnormalities of the subfoveal choriocapillaris.
source: For example, age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of severe vision loss in humans (de Jong, 2006) and is caused by abnormalities of the subfoveal choriocapillaris.
evidence: The claim is based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: Aldh1a1−/− and VAD mice would be useful to study regional differences in choroidal development and maintenance.
source: Aldh1a1−/− and VAD mice would be useful not only to study regional differences in choroidal development and maintenance but also to explore both a risk factor and a potential therapeutic target for AMD, because the RA concentration in the neural retina is affected by various environmental factors such as dietary intake of Vitamin A and light irradiation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the findings of the study and the potential relevance to AMD.

claim: Aldh1a1−/− and VAD mice would be useful to explore both a risk factor and a potential therapeutic target for AMD.
source: Aldh1a1−/− and VAD mice would be useful not only to study regional differences in choroidal development and maintenance but also to explore both a risk factor and a potential therapeutic target for AMD, because the RA concentration in the neural retina is affected by various environmental factors such as dietary intake of Vitamin A and light irradiation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the findings of the study and the potential relevance to AMD.

claim: The RA concentration in the neural retina is affected by various environmental factors such as dietary intake of Vitamin A and light irradiation.
source: Aldh1a1−/− and VAD mice would be useful not only to study regional differences in choroidal development and maintenance but also to explore both a risk factor and a potential therapeutic target for AMD, because the RA concentration in the neural retina is affected by various environmental factors such as dietary intake of Vitamin A and light irradiation.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about vitamin A metabolism and RA synthesis.

claim: RAs produced by Aldh1a1 in the neural retina direct dorsal choroidal vascular development via Sox9 upregulation in the dorsal RPE cells to enhance RPE-derived VEGF secretion.
source: These results suggest that RAs produced by Aldh1a1 in the neural retina directs dorsal choroidal vascular development via Sox9 upregulation in the dorsal RPE cells to enhance RPE-derived VEGF secretion.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from all the data presented.

claim: VEGF secreted from retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells is responsible for the choroidal vascular development.
source: VEGF secreted from retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells is responsible for the choroidal vascular development; however, the molecular regulatory mechanism is unclear.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge and supported by the context of the study.

claim: Aldh1a1–/– mice show choroidal hypoplasia with insufficient vascularization in the dorsal region.
source: We found that Aldh1a1–/– mice showed choroidal hypoplasia with insufficient vascularization in the dorsal region, although Aldh1a1, an enzyme that synthesizes retinoic acids (RAs), is expressed in the dorsal neural retina, not in the RPE/choroid complex.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the data presented.

claim: The level of VEGF in the RPE/choroid is significantly decreased in Aldh1a1–/– mice.
source: The level of VEGF in the RPE/choroid was significantly decreased in Aldh1a1–/– mice, and RA-dependent enhancement of VEGF was observed in primary RPE cells.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the ELISA data presented.

claim: RA-dependent enhancement of VEGF is observed in primary RPE cells.
source: The level of VEGF in the RPE/choroid was significantly decreased in Aldh1a1–/– mice, and RA-dependent enhancement of VEGF was observed in primary RPE cells.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the ELISA data presented.

claim: An RA-deficient diet results in dorsal choroidal hypoplasia.
source: An RA-deficient diet resulted in dorsal choroidal hypoplasia, and simple RA treatment of Aldh1a1–/– pregnant females suppressed choroid hypoplasia in their offspring.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the data from VAD mice.

claim: Simple RA treatment of Aldh1a1–/– pregnant females suppresses choroid hypoplasia in their offspring.
source: An RA-deficient diet resulted in dorsal choroidal hypoplasia, and simple RA treatment of Aldh1a1–/– pregnant females suppressed choroid hypoplasia in their offspring.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the data from RA-treated Aldh1a1–/– mice.

claim: Sox9 is downregulated in the dorsal neural retina and RPE of Aldh1a1–/– mice.
source: We also found downregulation of Sox9 in the dorsal neural retina and RPE of Aldh1a1–/– mice and RPE-specific disruption of Sox9 phenocopied Aldh1a1–/– choroidal development.
evidence: The claim is a key finding of the study, supported by the immunohistochemistry data presented.

claim: RPE-specific disruption of Sox9 phenocopies Aldh1a1–/– choroidal development.
source: We also found downregulation of Sox9 in the dorsal neural retina and RPE of Aldh1a1–/– mice and RPE-specific disruption of Sox9 phenocopied Aldh1a1–/– choroidal development.
